CrowdNode.description:
One anonymous device's live movement state.

node_id is a rotating pseudonym, not an identity. It is valid only within its rotation epoch and must never be joined across epochs.

epoch.description: ID rotation epoch; IDs are not comparable across epochs

node_id.description: rotating pseudonym, valid within its epoch only

zone_id.description: assigned by the state engine, not self-reported

NodeReport.description:
What a handset uploads.

Deliberately made of CrowdNode and nothing else. There are no anchor ids here, no RSSI, no scan lists: those are resolved on the phone and dropped. A report is a position, a speed and a heading under a rotating pseudonym — enough to count a crowd, not enough to follow a person.

Batched because uplinks are opportunistic (D7): a phone with no data connection keeps sensing and sends the backlog when it next has one.

consent_version.description: which disclosure this person actually agreed to. A report under an unknown consent version is rejected, not accepted-and-flagged.

node_id.description: rotating pseudonym, valid within its epoch only

nodes.description: one or more samples, oldest first

sources.description: which radios were usable while this batch was formed. Explains a coverage gap: 'the zone is empty' and 'every phone in the zone lost its anchor map' look identical without it.

Position.description:
A point in the venue's local metric frame, in metres.

Never latitude/longitude. Lat/lon exists only at the circuit pack's origin and at the device's location adapter (plan.md section 10).

PositionSource.description:
Which radio produced a position.

Not decorative and not merely diagnostic: accuracy differs by an order of magnitude between these, the confidence model weights on it, and an operator reading a sparse zone is entitled to know whether the dots there are GNSS fixes in the open or BLE fixes under a stand.
